We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 6 reactions, using templates in order: ['20810', '2895', '1914397', '1914398', '1914399', '74054'].

We have applied first three templates, got products (precursors). Need to continue applying remaining templates to appropriate molecules to eventually reach simple buyable starting materials.

We need to construct a tree JSON where each reaction node has children precursors (mol nodes). The order of templates must be as given, meaning first reaction uses template 20810 on target, producing two precursors. Then each of those precursors may be further broken down using next templates in order? Probably sequential chain: apply 20810 -> get two molecules A and B. Then apply 2895 to one of them (maybe the larger). Then apply 1914397 to resulting product, etc. Need total at least 6 reactions, using all six templates.

We have results:

After 20810: precursors: 
1) "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1"
2) "O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F" (that's a sulfonyl chloride with fluorophenyl)

Now apply 2895 to first precursor (we did) got product: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1" (only one product? It returned a tuple with one SMILES). So reaction yields that molecule (maybe plus something else but not shown). So after 2895 we have that molecule.

Now apply 1914397 to that molecule, got two products: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCNCC1" and "O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". So split into two fragments: a tert-butyl carbamate piperazine? Actually first is tBu carbamate piperazine (no aromatic). Second is a brominated phenyl fused with cyclohexanol.

Now we need to apply template 1914398 to one of these fragments (likely the aromatic bromide). Then 1914399 to next, then 74054 to final.

We need to see what these templates do, but we don't have description. We'll attempt to apply them sequentially to appropriate molecules.

First, apply 1914398 to the aromatic fragment "O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2".
